preamble: Click loss replaces the nasal alveolar click [ŋǃ] (written nǃ) with a plain velar nasal [ŋ]: the anterior alveolar closure and the velaric suction are dropped, and only the rear velar closure with its nasal accompaniment survives. The case is Kua, an Eastern Kalahari Khoe language of Botswana, where words with nǃ in click-retaining Gǀui have initial ŋ. Its sisters Cua and Tsua have plain k or g in the same words, without the nasal, so Kua shows the nasal reflex of the same click-loss process. The entry is filed under the alveolar click [ǃ] with its nasal accompaniment. The change is confined to one language, so it is rare.

examples.note: The nasal alveolar click is reduced to a velar nasal; Cua and Tsua have kua, without the nasal.
